request.spec:
Claims can be selected (a checkbox on each) and opened together with one button. Each selected
claim that can be opened is opened and numbered in list order (the list order of people, newest
claim first within a person); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were opened and
how many were refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Claims can be selected (a checkbox on each) and opened together with one button. Each selected
claim that can be opened is opened and numbered in list order (the list order of people, newest
claim first within a person); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were opened and
how many were refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk open now works: each claim has a checkbox, and an "Open selected" button opens all the ticked claims and shows how many were opened and how many were refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the bulk-open test and the three scenario tests), and the TypeScript typecheck is clean.

I only changed the front end, in three new files under `src/main/frontend/features/claims/`:
- **`useSelectedClaims.ts`** keeps the ticked claim ids in the URL (`selectedClaims`), which is how DESIGN.md says selection state should be held.
- **`select.slot.tsx`** adds the `claim-select` checkbox as the first cell of each claim row.
- **`bulkOpen.slot.tsx`** is the panel with the `bulk-open` button and the `bulk-opened` / `bulk-refused` counts.

How it behaves:
- **Order and numbering:** the ticked claims are sorted in list order (people as listed, newest claim first within each person). Each one is then opened through the existing single-claim open endpoint, one at a time, so the numbers follow that order.
- **Reuses the existing rules:** because it goes through the same endpoint, every refusal rule and audit record is unchanged. A claim that can't be opened (already open, in a closed period, and so on) is left as it is and counted as refused. Each opened claim writes the same audit lines as a single open would.
- **Counts:** the old counts disappear when the button is pressed and the new ones appear when the run is done. The selection is cleared afterwards.

The run is not all-or-nothing. If one claim is refused, the others that could be opened are still opened, which is what the request asks for. But it also means that if the run is interrupted (a network failure, say), the claims already opened stay open.
